[quote=dhornaper;59860994]General Fereydun watches the last day of the military exercises unfold with some impatience. He taps his foot as he watches some of his men from his seat on a nearby hill. He abruptly says "take notes" to the chief of staff before beginning his observations.

"From what I've seen, the men know cover and concealment well, they can exploit the variations of the earth to hide and take cover and are sufficiently dispersed.

The first problem I see is that small units have trouble maneuvering well because their ability to provide covering fire is weak. The men need to be trained to judge their next position better, see their neighbour's next position, and provide enough covering fire. The time and effects of crossing open ground between positions then is lessened.

The next is where things will get difficult. The infantry work well with the artillery but communication on target locations isn't good enough. The artillery can do suppressive fire on static targets but changing to a new target is slow and accuracy of hitting moving targets poor.

The infantry works well with mechanised units but again, it's the artillery.

Now, you'll need to ask the air staff chief on problems with the air force since that's not my expertise. I want you and him to attend the other planned exercises across the country and watch for the same issues spotted here. I'm heading back to Shar to reorganise the government and draft reforms from what I've spotted here."

With his observations complete, he leaves for Shar as the exercises wind down.

Mr. Achebe sits fiddling with his pen, staring out a seaview window of the cafe he has chosen for lunch. He seems tense and preoccupied, leaving his meal mostly untouched and worrying his brother. Turning to him, he asks Martin, what do you think of the recent coup? His brother is slightly caught off guard mid-bite into his sandwich, however he chews and takes time to ponder the question. Which one? Martin retorts as he takes a small drink from his flask. The one in Dhornaper. Martin takes longer to think about a response this time, but provides an adequate one. I think while its not the best, they still haven't done anything too rash. I dont have a clue what they are gonna do with the remnants of the old administration, or how well their new picks will run the country. Mr. Achebe finally touches his food, biting a croissant in half, nodding as his brother speaks. Im thinking of scheduling a diplomatic mission to them with the Shamat Ambassador as the main visitor. Even if it ends poorly, I wish to at least be able to guess their agenda. Why not go yourself? Martin asks. It is important, no? Mr Achebe nods slightly. I wish to attend the funeral of the president of [nation]New Westmore[/nation]. There hasnt been any information on when it is though, so I wish to keep my schedule mostly open and this would be a big commitment.

Martin stands up and checks his watch. Thank you for inviting me to lunch man, but I have to pick my son from moms house. She always says he reminds her of you. Mr Achebe stands up and smiles. I hope not. She still remembers when I tried to jump in the pool from the second story window. With that, the meeting ends, and Mr. Achebe takes his lunch to go as he thinks of the best way to go about this mission.
